messages.subject: Multilevel Modelling
parts:
Hi,

I want to model life expectancy using two covariates unemployment rate and education level within states of a country. I want the the covariates to have different effect in each state on the life expectancy. So this is how I wrote the formula: 

##################### R code #####################
formula = life_expectancy ~ -1 +
  f(state, unemployment_rate) +
  f(state, education_level )
################################################

But I am getting this error: 

Error in inla.interpret.formula(formula, data.same.len = data.same.len, : The covariate `state' are used in the following f()-terms: 1, 2 Only one is allowed since the naming convention of the f()-terms depends on unique names of the covariates 
 You can resolve this as follows: Not allowed: formula = y ~ f(x, <etc>) + f(x, <etc>) + <etc> Fix: data$xx = data$x; formula = y ~ f(x, <etc>) + f(xx, <etc>) + <etc> 

So according the suggestion in the error I have to create another column in my dataset identical to "state" only with different name. Is that necessary? Why INLA can't work similar to other packages that can run formula = life_expectancy ~ -1 +(unemployment_rate | state) + (education_level | state)?

Best,
Amin

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Multilevel Modelling
parts:
if you use 'f()', then the name of that model component is defined
through the name of the first argument, so

... + f(x,... ) + f(x,....)

does not work, but if you set

data$xx = data$x

then use

... + f(x, ...) + f(xx, ...)

instead
